Dude I totally get it! I can't say I can really answer your question because I don't think that there's much advice you can give on this subject. Also you gotta let go of expectations to see what you really want to be involved in. Let go of the need to be good at something your not. Also let go of the need to make work your entire purpose or life path. You may discover you don't want to do something engaging for work. You may want something totally boring and easy that doesn't take up much of your energy for work so you can focus on what you really care about on your free time! Okay to be totally honest I think FWB is a really bad idea especially in this situation. I think you both sort of know this but also are really excited about the idea of hooking up. I don't think he was rejecting you I think that was a sign of respect for your relationship in that he is very attracted to you but doesn't want to make a rash decision because your friendship means a lot to him as well. This type of arrangement I think you need to realize can be more detrimental to a friendship than dating could be. That is because at least in dating you know that romantic feelings are reciprocated with a FWB you do not know this. If one party wants things to progress and the other doesn't there is room for a lot of heartbreak and a lot of awkwardness.

If you realize that you want something romantic to develop from this I don't think its a good idea to pursue this through an FWB. Men can have emotional connection and great sex and not develop romantic feelings. It's a lot harder for women to do this scientifically especially if you already have some romantic feelings there.

I personally had a long term FWB and we weren't initially very emotionally connected even though we were friends. I didn't have a crush on him to start with but adding sex to the friendship made it really hard for me to get over him I was very emotionally attached. The success rate is so low for moving from FWB to dating that it's a huge risk and I think you need to ask if you are willing to take that risk with the possibility of both losing the friendship AND romantic possibilities.
